note: 17 Nov 2026 - second pass of 'Improving Relationships & Top 10 Motivational Speakers Of All-Time | The Kevin Trudeau Show | Ep.17' (Rumble v4y99ab). The relationship half of the episode is off-lane (skipped by the prep filter) and the motivational-speakers countdown is almost entirely archival audio of OTHER people (Jim Rohn, Zig Ziglar, Earl Nightingale, Les Brown, Charlie Jones, Ron Ball, Ed Foreman, Bob Harrington, Norman Vincent Peale) - Kevin introduces each clip but does not talk through them, which fails KEVIN IS THE CLIP. The only clean, self-contained Kevin-only stretch that survives is the opening of his 'success triangle' story (books/audios/events), used by WHY-SUCCESSFUL-PEOPLE-NEED-A-PARTNER from 1482s on. Cut just the 'books' third of it, stopping before the Global Information Network club-membership plug and the KevinTrudeaufanclub.com mention. The rest of the triangle (audios, events/secret-society) and the closing 'I don't get paid for this, it goes to pay the lawyers' segment were left out: the first two run straight into the club pitch or a long Bible tangent inside the 190s cap, and the last touches his legal/financial history, which is not a lesson for the viewer. One clean arc survived; fewer good clips beat more weak ones. Weekly agent.

clips.start_words: When I was in the brotherhood
clips.send: A reader just finishing a self-help book sends this to a skeptical friend, pure awe that a 700-year-old order already knew the trick.
clips.caption:
Kevin Trudeau says the real secret to success was never really secret - it goes back to the Knights Templar, thousands of years before self-help books existed.

He was taught the same system: reading isn't just information. Positive, motivational material stimulates parts of the brain other activities don't reach.

That matters, he says, because what you focus on is what you broadcast - and what you broadcast tends to show up.

Most people wait for proof before trying something new. The people who built real fortunes read first, and believed on the way there.

What's the last book that actually changed how you think?
